author: /root/rust_scheduler_fp_admission_cutover
scope: Functional supported-profile kernel and apps; independent Rust scheduler FPU-admission unsafe/IRQ/ABI/default-consumer source and extracted-object review. No implementation ownership, no native acceptance.
language_boundary: New selected compute-kernel behavior is Rust with existing assembly/ABI bridges. Corrected C prelude remains exact fallback/reference; no expanded C behavior.
reasoning: Existing process_sched_irq_save_bridge disables IRQs before processor lookup, CPU-local lookup, no_preempt/current/status observation or save. Raw pointer formation avoids constructing exclusive Rust references to shared CPU/thread objects. SeqCst AtomicI32 read matches existing ihk_atomic_read and 4-byte aligned CInt counter ABI.

CPU-local current cannot be locally rescheduled between IRQ exclusion and existing preparation. The port adds no new lock ordering: it takes no runqueue lock before save. Existing remote status and lifetime assumptions are preserved rather than widened.

Short-circuit tests preserve no_preempt(nonzero including negative), null, idle and exited exclusions. Any nonzero save return invokes the actual nonvariadic panic ABI with a NUL-terminated static message and Rust never return type; no restore, prepare or queue mutation is reachable after failure.
Existing panic only stops the calling CPU, not all CPUs. This retained limitation is stated and not expanded into global safety acceptance.

C default path calls the helper exactly once before sched_schedule_prepare_body_result. Nested IRQ-save during preparation sees IRQs already disabled. Non-switch C restore uses original entry flags; switch path replaces runq_irqstate with original entry flags while runqueue lock and IRQ exclusion remain held, preserving existing migration-aware unlock/restore continuation.

Extern C int/i32, unsigned long/u64 on supported x86_64, pointer/usize/u64 bridge return, and panic const-char-pointer types agree. Complete Rust Thread/CpuLocalVar ABI module and its compile assertions were compiled; retained C fixture asserts matching selected sizes/offsets. Full production C/header compile remains pending.

Frozen C fallback hash, retained poisoned pre-IRQ fields, all 32 child statuses/streams and complete artifact hashes verify. The inspected Rust object has ordered IRQ-save/local lookup/loads/save/panic and no SIMD instructions. These controls support bounded source/object parity only.

Default ENABLE_RUST_KERNEL ON, process.c macro definition and sched_helpers module inclusion establish source selection. Extracted selected C object references new helper and fallback does not; complete target linking has not yet established whole-image symbol closure.
next_build_conditions: Dispatcher packages exact reviewed process.c/sched_helpers.rs and matching separately reviewed FPU-copy cpu.c/x86_cpu_helpers.rs sources; bind complete source, IHK/config and pinned toolchain identities.
Run full actual target Rust crate and production C compilation with supported profile feature cfgs and existing no-SIMD kernel flags; resolve every symbol without duplicate definitions.
Inspect linked image/default process schedule consumer and helper/save/panic/IRQ bridge ownership; confirm no fallback C admission executes under default Rust selection.

Native startup and relevant FPU/scheduling/error evidence require current separately valid heavy execution release, resource lease, complete capture and verified teardown; this review does not release guest/root work.
